$comment: Brand content for the catalog: what Fourthwall doesn't hold (internal design code, release, position, category, Scripture, copy). When a product's slug (or fourthwallSlug) matches a public Fourthwall product, Fourthwall supplies its variants, prices and stock. Until then the product shows as a preview with the price and sizes here, and ordering not yet open. `images` are always the site's own (apps/web/public/products): Fourthwall's product renders, or the approved mockup, on each piece's styled surface, made by assets/mockups. `scripture` is each piece's shared Scripture record: the website shows one translation (SCRIPTURE_TRANSLATION, NIV by default) everywhere the piece appears. `code` is internal and never shown to customers. `colors` maps garment color names to brand swatch tokens. `images` are listed in display order: listing image (the whole garment), hover image, then the rest.

collections.name: Behold
collections.tagline: Clothes that ask you to look at Jesus, and keep looking.
collections.story: “Behold” is an old word for look, and keep looking. It’s the word older English Bibles use when John the Baptist sees Jesus walking toward him and points Him out to the crowd: “Behold the Lamb of God.” Each piece in this release points to who Jesus is and what He has done. He makes scarlet sins white as snow. He gives a life worth living. He healed the woman who touched His cloak. On the third day the stone was rolled away. He calmed the storm, and His death tore the temple veil. He walks with us through the darkest valley, He made us with care, and He is the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.

scripture.kjv: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow

story.art: A crown of thorns breaks into lilies around the wordmark, under a cross.
story.meaning: Through Isaiah, God invites His people to come and settle things with Him, and promises that sins red as scarlet will be made white as snow. The crown of thorns is what that mercy cost. The lilies are what grows from it. The print is deep red on a pale ecru shirt, the scarlet and the snow of the verse.

scripture.niv: For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
scripture.kjv: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

story.art: An hourglass holds a cross above and a sprouting seed below, between the words of Philippians 1:21.
story.meaning: Paul wrote this from prison, not knowing whether he would be released or executed, and decided he couldn’t lose either way. If he lived, he would keep serving Christ. If he died, he would be with Him. The hourglass holds a cross above and a sprouting seed below, time running out and a life that keeps going.

scripture.niv: If I only touch his cloak, I will be healed.
scripture.kjv: If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole.

story.art: A woman’s hand reaches through a spray of rust to take hold of the edge of a cloak, beside the words she said to herself.
story.meaning: She had been bleeding for twelve years, and nothing had helped. She didn’t ask Jesus for anything. She came up behind Him in the crowd and touched the edge of His cloak, sure that would be enough. Jesus turned, saw her, and told her that her faith had healed her. The back shows her hand closing on the cloak, with her words above it.

scripture.niv: He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.

story.art: The stone rolls away in a sweep of blue under the angel’s words.
story.meaning: At dawn on the first day of the week, an angel rolled the stone away from the tomb and sat on it. He told the women who had come that Jesus wasn’t there. He had risen, just as He said. The back prints the angel’s words in heavy capitals, plain as a headline, with the stone still rolling in a sweep of blue. The front keeps only the wordmark.

scripture.kjv: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom

story.meaning: When Jesus died on the cross, the curtain in the temple that closed off the Most Holy Place tore in two, from top to bottom. It tore from the top, from God’s side. Through Christ’s death, the way into God’s presence is open. The back shows the curtain torn wide with light coming through. The front carries the wordmark and the Thorn Cross.

scripture.niv: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me
scripture.kjv: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me

story.art: One traveler walks a narrow, lit path through a dark valley toward a cross on the hill, under a full moon and the words “I will fear no evil.”
story.meaning: David knew dark valleys. He kept sheep in the wild as a boy, and later spent years running from a king who wanted him dead. In Psalm 23 he writes that even in the darkest valley he won’t be afraid, because the Lord is with him, guiding and guarding him like a shepherd with his rod and staff. Jesus later called Himself the good shepherd. The back shows one traveler on the path through the valley, walking toward the cross.

story.meaning: In Psalm 139, David is amazed at how completely God knows him: every thought, every word, every day of his life, written down before one of them came to be. God formed him in his mother’s womb, and David answers with praise, because he is fearfully and wonderfully made. The back sets those words among roses in bloom around a wooden cross. The front carries the wordmark and the Thorn Cross in deep red.

scripture.niv: Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
scripture.kjv: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

story.art: The Lamb of God in white thread inside a red crown of thorns, with one mark of red on the lamb.
story.meaning: When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming toward him, he pointed Him out to the crowd as the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. Older English Bibles begin John’s words with “Behold,” and this release takes its name from them. The lamb is stitched in white inside a red crown of thorns, with a single mark of red. The wordmark sits on the back.

scripture.niv: In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins
scripture.kjv: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins

story.art: The Awebound wordmark embroidered in white, outlined and thorned in deep red, above a small Thorn Cross.
story.meaning: This is the everyday Awebound cap: the wordmark and the Thorn Cross, nothing more. The red along the thorns means the same thing as the Lamb’s Mark. It stands for the sacrifice of our Lord Jesus Christ, who wore a crown of thorns and gave His life for us. Through His blood we are forgiven.
